messages.subject: Qmatrix
parts:
Hi Nick,

Stacey and I were trying to do the stochastic mapping (simulate_biogeog_history) and we see that we need some things we don't know how to get - the Qmatrix, the speciation/transition matrix. We thought that for determining the most likely types of range shifts, just looking at the Qmatrix would be informative.  If the stochastic mapping is a while in coming, is it easy to pull out the Qmatrix just to look at it?
Thanks!!

Julia

I'm traveling and this is gas station internet, but briefly - iirc that function does a forward simulation given a tree  & model, but that's a different thing from stochastic mapping, and both of those are different from a joint simulation of the tree & the biogeography with an SSE type model. I have code for all 3 but I think the code for the only the first is online. Stochastic mapping is guaranteed to produce your observed ranges at the tips  while the forward simulations almost certainly will not...should be online some over the holiday weekend...

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Qmatrix
parts:
Back in the office but still catching up -- another thought on this: the Q matrix will tell you about the oveall rates of the anagenetic range-changing events, but not the cladogenetic range-changing events.  There are ways to get the cladogenesis range-changing matrix, but it's in a special format, it would take some time to add it to the tutorial.  It wouldn't be too hard to figure out by digging through the likelihood code in BioGeoBEARS. But even with those, usually people would be interested in which events between which areas are happening during which time slices.  The transition matrices just give the overall abstract probabilities, not the events at specific points on the tree.  

Cheers!
Nick
